sections.text:
**Considering SEO tools**

I need to figure out if using web tools can help answer current SEO and AIO questions. There’s a lot to look into, and recommendations on the latest practices would really come in handy. I should probably browse different sources to gather relevant information and insights. Finding up-to-date recommendations will be crucial to ensure clarity and effectiveness in addressing SEO strategies.

To get your website cited by AI search engines, think less “trick the AI” and more **become the clearest, most trustworthy, easiest-to-retrieve source for specific questions**. AI citations usually come from the same ingredients as strong SEO: crawlability, authority, clarity, topical depth, and useful original information.

Here’s a practical checklist.

## 1. Make sure AI/search crawlers can access your site

If AI systems can’t crawl your pages, they can’t cite them.

Check your `robots.txt` and firewall/CDN rules. At minimum, do **not accidentally block** major search crawlers or AI search crawlers you want visibility from.

For Google AI Overviews, Google says normal SEO fundamentals still apply and that you do **not** need a special “AI file,” special markup, or separate opt-in to appear in AI features. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features?utm_source=openai))

For ChatGPT Search, OpenAI says publishers may need to allow **OAI-SearchBot** in `robots.txt`; it also distinguishes search access from training access, so you can allow search discovery without necessarily allowing all training crawlers. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856-publishers-and-developers-faq%23%3A~%3Atext%3DChatGPT%20automatically%20includes%20the%20UTM%20parameter%20utm_source%3Dchatgpt.com%20in%20referral%20URLs%2C%20enabling%20clear%20tracking%20and%20analysis%20of%20inbound%20traffic%20from%20ChatGPT%20search%20results?utm_source=openai))

Example:

```txt
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /
```

That example allows OpenAI’s search crawler while opting out of GPTBot training access. Verify this against your own legal/content policy.

## 2. Get indexed in Google and Bing

AI answers often draw from search indexes. So the basics matter:

- Submit XML sitemaps.
- Use Google Search Console.
- Use Bing Webmaster Tools.
- Fix crawl errors.
- Avoid noindex tags on pages you want cited.
- Make sure canonical tags are correct.
- Use fast, accessible HTML, not content hidden behind scripts.

Bing now has an **AI Performance** report in Bing Webmaster Tools that shows how your content is used in AI-generated answers across Microsoft Copilot and related experiences, including cited pages and grounding queries. ([bing.com](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/ai-performance-9f8e7d6c?utm_source=openai))

## 3. Create “citation-worthy” pages, not generic blog posts

AI engines cite pages that help support a specific answer. Your content should make it easy for an AI system to extract a clear, reliable claim.

Good citation-worthy pages usually include:

- A direct answer near the top.
- Clear headings phrased like real user questions.
- Short, self-contained explanation sections.
- Original data, examples, comparisons, screenshots, or definitions.
- Author credentials or company expertise.
- Dates updated and version history where relevant.
- Sources for claims.
- Clear product, service, or methodology details.

Bad pages for AI citation:

- Vague thought-leadership fluff.
- Thin listicles.
- Over-optimized keyword pages.
- Pages with no clear answer.
- Content copied from competitors.
- Content that buries the useful answer 1,000 words down.

## 4. Target question-style and comparison queries

AI search is especially likely to answer queries like:

- “What is the best way to…”
- “How does X compare to Y?”
- “Is X worth it for Y?”
- “What are the requirements for…”
- “How much does X cost?”
- “What are the risks of…”
- “What is the difference between…”

Create pages around **specific buyer, research, and troubleshooting questions** in your niche.

Example structure:

```md
# X vs Y: Which is better for [specific audience]?

Short answer: X is usually better for [case], while Y is better for [case].

## Quick comparison table

## When to choose X

## When to choose Y

## Cost comparison

## Limitations

## Our recommendation

## FAQ
```

This format gives AI systems clean passages to cite.

## 5. Build topical authority

One isolated article is less likely to be cited than a site with a strong cluster of related content.

For example, if you sell cybersecurity software, don’t just publish:

- “Best cybersecurity tools”

Also publish:

- “What is endpoint detection and response?”
- “EDR vs MDR”
- “SOC 2 cybersecurity requirements”
- “How to respond to a phishing attack”
- “Cybersecurity checklist for small businesses”
- “Incident response plan template”
- “Ransomware recovery steps”

Then internally link them together.

AI systems are more likely to trust you when your site demonstrates depth across the topic.

## 6. Add structured data, but don’t rely on it alone

Schema markup can help search engines understand your pages, though it is not a magic AI citation switch.

Useful schema types may include:

- `Article`
- `FAQPage`
- `HowTo`
- `Product`
- `Organization`
- `Person`
- `Review`
- `SoftwareApplication`
- `LocalBusiness`
- `Dataset`

Also make sure your organization/entity information is consistent across your site, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn, Crunchbase, Wikidata if relevant, industry directories, and review platforms.

## 7. Publish original facts AI can cite

If you want AI systems to cite you, give them something worth citing.

Examples:

- Original research.
- Industry surveys.
- Benchmarks.
- Pricing studies.
- Case studies.
- First-party data.
- Calculators.
- Templates.
- Expert interviews.
- Regulatory explainers.
- Technical documentation.
- Glossaries.
- Comparison tables.

AI search engines often need sources to support factual claims. If your page contains unique, well-presented facts, it has a better chance of becoming that source.

## 8. Use clear extractable formatting

Make your pages easy for machines and humans to parse.

Use:

- Descriptive H2s and H3s.
- Summary boxes.
- Tables.
- Bullets.
- Definitions.
- FAQs.
- Step-by-step instructions.
- Concise answer paragraphs.
- Descriptive image alt text.
- Clean HTML.

Avoid:

- Huge walls of text.
- Ambiguous headings like “Our Thoughts.”
- Important information only in images.
- Popups blocking content.
- Infinite-scroll-only content.
- Pages that require login for the useful answer.

## 9. Earn mentions and links from authoritative sites

AI search systems often prefer sources that are already trusted on the open web.

Ways to build authority:

- Get cited by industry publications.
- Contribute expert commentary.
- Publish original studies others reference.
- Appear in niche directories.
- Get reviews on credible platforms.
- Build high-quality backlinks.
- Maintain consistent brand/entity profiles.
- Encourage customers and partners to mention your brand naturally.

Traditional SEO authority still matters because AI search systems often use search ranking, link signals, and known-source trust as part of retrieval.

## 10. Track AI visibility separately from normal SEO

Monitor:

- Google Search Console queries where AI Overviews appear.
- Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance.
- Referral traffic from `chatgpt.com`, `perplexity.ai`, `copilot.microsoft.com`, etc.
- Brand mentions in AI answers.
- Which competitors are being cited.
- Which pages get cited versus ignored.
- Which query types produce citations.

OpenAI notes that ChatGPT can include `utm_source=chatgpt.com` in referral URLs, which can help publishers track ChatGPT traffic in analytics tools. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856-publishers-and-developers-faq%23%3A~%3Atext%3DChatGPT%20automatically%20includes%20the%20UTM%20parameter%20utm_source%3Dchatgpt.com%20in%20referral%20URLs%2C%20enabling%20clear%20tracking%20and%20analysis%20of%20inbound%20traffic%20from%20ChatGPT%20search%20results?utm_source=openai))

## 11. Create pages for “source intent,” not just “buyer intent”

A lot of AI citations come from informational pages, not landing pages.

Instead of only optimizing:

- “Buy accounting software”

Also create:

- “What does accounting software do?”
- “Accounting software pricing guide”
- “Best accounting software for nonprofits”
- “How to migrate from spreadsheets to accounting software”
- “Cash vs accrual accounting explained”
- “Accounting software implementation checklist”

Then link those educational pages to your commercial pages.

## 12. Keep pages fresh

AI search favors current, reliable information for topics that change.

Add:

- “Last updated” dates.
- Current pricing.
- Current screenshots.
- Updated statistics.
- Current regulations.
- Version notes.
- Deprecated-information warnings.

Don’t fake freshness. Actually update the content.

---

# Quick 30-day plan

## Week 1: Technical access

- Check `robots.txt`.
- Allow important crawlers.
- Submit sitemaps to Google and Bing.
- Fix indexing issues.
- Set up Bing Webmaster Tools and Google Search Console.
- Check server logs for crawler access.

## Week 2: Content audit

Identify 20–50 high-value questions your customers ask. For each, check:

- Do you have a page answering it?
- Is the answer clear in the first few paragraphs?
- Is the page more useful than competitors?
- Does it include original insight or data?
- Is it internally linked?

## Week 3: Create citation assets

Build or improve:

- Comparison pages.
- FAQ pages.
- How-to guides.
- Glossary pages.
- Original data pages.
- Templates or calculators.
- Case studies.

## Week 4: Authority and measurement

- Promote your strongest assets.
- Pitch journalists or industry newsletters.
- Add expert bylines.
- Improve internal linking.
- Track AI citations manually and in Bing’s AI Performance report.
- Watch referral traffic from AI platforms.

---
